pr_title: Move project-specific editor data into res://.godot/editor
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/282, follow up to #38607, fixes #42578. This PR moves the project-specific editor data files into a subfolder of `res://.godot` called `res://.godot/editor` (defined as a constant: `EditorSettings::EDITOR_FILES_PATH`). 

One advantage of this change is that it's easy to delete a project without leaving any files behind. Another advantage is that if you screw up the editor settings for your project, it's very easy to reset them by deleting `res://.godot` (or just `res://.godot/editor`). A third advantage is that if you move a project to a different location, your editor settings are still there (previously the editor settings were stored in a location with the MD5 sum of the project path, so if the path changes then you lose the settings).

A change that people may or may not see as an advantage is that if you ZIP up a project without deleting the `res://.godot/editor` folder, you will share the project-specific editor settings with the recipient of that ZIP file, so they should see exactly what you see (in terms of editor layout, but not non-project-specific settings like the theme or font size).

A question remains about whether or not this should be configurable. It makes the code a lot simpler to just make it always inside the project, but maybe some people wouldn't like this behavior.
pr_comments:
@Xrayez Alternatively, we could either expose the constant itself, or we could encourage users to pick their own folder inside of `.godot` like `.godot/myplugin`.

Also, AFAIK, the method can't be explicitly inlined if it's also exposed, because of how inlining works.

I guess a method like this (but probably not called `get_project_settings_dir`) can return the root of `res://.godot` instead. Though, arguably, at this point there is not a lot of use in a function for looking up a folder which is discoverable as `res://.godot`.

> Alternatively, we could either expose the constant itself, or we could encourage users to pick their own folder inside of `.godot` like `.godot/myplugin`.

I just think there are many similar methods currently accessible via the `EditorInterface` in the same manner, which have the pattern of `get_*_path`, so I'd think twice before removing *editor interface* methods which are exposed specifically for convenience purpose, like improving the editor traversal.

For instance, it's possible to access the `EditorNode` root and do `get_child()` to get the base, other plugins etc:
```gdscript
var base = get_tree().get_root().get_child(0) # This might not be the base, but you get the point.
```

Plugins like https://github.com/Zylann/godot_editor_debugger_plugin take advantage of this ability, in fact.

But doing so via `EditorInterface` simplifies this task currently:
```gdscript
var base = get_editor_interface().get_base_control()
```
So the main purpose of those methods is exactly convenience, in my opinion. If adding a constant helps to avoid quite verbose `EditorSettings->get_singleton()->get_project_settings_dir()` in C++, then should be ok, as long as `get_project_settings_dir` is retained.

The pros and cons for this are also described in godotengine/godot-proposals#70.

EDIT: the examples with `EditorInterface` are probably outside of the scope of `EditorSettings`, but the same reasoning still applies.

---

Plugins themselves could also have their respective folder, like `.godot/plugins/myplugin` or `.godot/editor/plugins/myplugin`. Building upon pycbouch's idea, `get_plugin_settings_dir` could also be added, although it may be that not every plugin would need to store plugin-related settings. Plugin names can be uniquely inferred from `addons/` currently.

> Also, AFAIK, the method can't be explicitly inlined if it's also exposed, because of how inlining works.

Making method calls inline would only work at compile-time for C++ usage, I think it shouldn't affect GDScript calls, but it's likely not performance-critical anyways.

> I guess a method like this (but probably not called `get_project_settings_dir`) can return the root of `res://.godot` instead. Though, arguably, at this point there is not a lot of use in a function for looking up a folder which is discoverable as `res://.godot`.

`get_project_settings_dir` can also be renamed to `get_project_editor_settings_dir` if we aim at breaking compatibility completely, then again my main concern is retaining the method to be usable in scripts.

Or rename the `EditorSettings::EDITOR_FILES_PATH` to `EditorSettings::PROJECT_EDITOR_SETTINGS_DIR` and expose as a constant.
@Xrayez What do you think of this PR in its current state?
Just noting that I like the idea, I'll test the PR and review the above discussion more in-depth before approving.

issue_context.title: Favorites from a deleted project in a new one with the same name
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
v3.2.3.stable.official

**OS/device including version:**
macOS Catalina 10.15.5

**Issue description:**
When you delete a project and create a new one with the same name in the same folder, Godot uses favorites from the deleted project. The same might be true for some of the cache files stored in " /Users/marcin/Library/Application\ Support/Godot/projects". 

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Create a new project
2. Create a new folder
3. Create a new scene and save it in the folder
4. Add scene to favorites
5. Save the project and close Godot
6. Delete the project folder
7. Open Godot and remove the missing project
8. Create a new project with the same name in the same folder
comments: This is because the project-specific editor data is stored for each unique project path. And it is never removed, unless you go into the editor data directory and manually delete it. This will be fixed in #42394 by moving this data into a special folder at the project root.

> This is because the project-specific editor data is stored for each unique project path. And it is never removed, unless you go into the editor data directory and manually delete it. This will be fixed in #42394 by moving this data into a special folder at the project root.

Thank a lot for the response! I guess I can close this issue then.

review_comments: Since there's a getter for it specifically, maybe it doesn't need to be a separate constant? You could just use `get_project_settings_dir()` in `create()`.
The original idea was to remove the methods and only have the constant, but the method is still needed if we want to expose this (we can't bind string constants AFAIK, just numeric ones).
